disclaimer: This catalogue tells you a subgraph EXISTS and what we saw from ONE query at the stated timestamp. It is not a certification that it works now. ALWAYS run the freshness probe yourself before relying on any entry.
howToTest: POST the freshnessProbe to gatewayUrl with an Authorization: Bearer <Subgraph Studio key> header. Compare _meta.block.number against the chain head. A stale or empty response means do not rely on it, regardless of queryFeesGrt.

Note cost is raw wei (0.000163 ETH and 0.00198 ETH here), not USD, and registrationDate/expiryDate/ttl are raw unix seconds - consumers must apply decimals themselves. entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } deployment hasIndexingErrors } pools(first: 3, orderBy: volumeUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id token0 { symbol } token1 { symbol } volumeUSD feesUSD totalValueLockedUSD txCount } }
entries.fieldWarning: Values are plausible (no trillion-dollar TVL, no zero-volume top row; top pool fee/volume ratio 0.026% is sane). Two naming traps instead: (1) this Algebra fork kept Polygon field names on an Arbitrum deployment - Bundle.maticPriceUSD returned 2514.31, which is the ETH price, not MATIC, and likewise derivedMatic / totalValueLockedMatic / volumeMatic / totalVolumeMatic are ETH-denominated; reading them as MATIC is wrong by ~3 orders of magnitude. (2) Pool 0xc86eb7b85807020b4548ee05b54bfc956eebbfcd reports both token0.symbol and token1.symbol as "USDC" (bridged USDC.e vs native USDC) - disambiguate by token id, never by symbol. Soft anomaly, not treated as a bug: that same pool shows $83.4k feesUSD on $9.91B volumeUSD (0.00084%), ~5x below the USDC/USDT pool's ratio - explicable for a near-zero dynamic fee stable pair.
entries.note: Live Camelot V3 (Algebra) concentrated-liquidity DEX data on Arbitrum One — pools, swaps, ticks, positions and TVL/volume; verified synced at Arbitrum block 505,256,254 with 1,536 pools and ~$6.5M TVL.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } pools(first: 3, orderBy: volumeUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id feeTier volumeUSD totalValueLockedUSD txCount token0 { symbol } token1 { symbol } } }
entries.fieldWarning: totalValueLockedUSD is unreliable on this deployment. The 0.3% pool (0x6c561b44...1372) reports $179.3M TVL versus only $32.7M for the 0.05% pool that does ~3x its volume and 6x its tx count — an inverted, implausible ranking. A follow-up query showed the USD value is internally consistent with its reserves (34,536.35 WETH x $2,512.18 ethPriceUSD + 92,797,839 USDC = $179.5M) and totalValueLockedUSDUntracked is 0, so the inflation lives in the underlying totalValueLockedToken0/token1 accumulators — the known Uniswap V3 subgraph burn/collect accounting drift that compounds on high-tx-count pools. Do not rank or size pools by totalValueLockedUSD here; rank by volumeUSD or feesUSD, which returned sane, correctly ordered, nonzero values.
entries.note: Canonical Uniswap V3 pool/swap/liquidity data on Base — pools, ticks, positions, and USD volume/TVL time series (1.88M pools, $172B cumulative volume), synced live to Base head.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number } } pairs(first: 3, orderBy: trackedReserveETH, orderDirection: desc) { id token0 { symbol } token1 { symbol } trackedReserveETH reserveUSD volumeUSD txCount } }
entries.fieldWarning: Pair.reserveUSD is a junk ranking field on this subgraph — DO NOT use orderBy: reserveUSD. An actual run of `pairs(first: 3, orderBy: reserveUSD, orderDirection: desc)` returned three untracked scam pairs (TPAD/unknown, ZKLK/unknown, unknown/0xDEV), each reporting reserveUSD = 8796331383679371216730568536244296 (~8.8e33 USD, i.e. trillions-of-trillions) while volumeUSD = "0", txCount = "3", and trackedReserveETH = "0". These are unpriced/untracked tokens whose USD reserves are fabricated by the pricing logic. Rank by trackedReserveETH (whitelist-tracked liquidity) instead — reserveUSD is still fine to READ as a display value on a pair already selected via trackedReserveETH.
entries.note: Canonical Uniswap V2 Ethereum mainnet subgraph — pairs, swaps, mints/burns, token and factory-level TVL/volume aggregates; live query returned factory 0x5C69bEe7 with 521,972 pairs and $865.7B lifetime volume.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } pools(first: 3, orderBy: volumeUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id feeTier volumeUSD feesUSD txCount totalValueLockedUSD token0 { symbol } token1 { symbol } } }

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number } } uniswapDayDatas(first: 3, orderBy: date, orderDirection: desc) { id date volumeUSD feesUSD tvlUSD txCount } }
entries.fieldWarning: Two issues. (1) UniswapDayData.txCount is cumulative all-time, NOT daily, despite the schema comment "number of daily transactions" — consecutive days returned 247,822,156 / 247,818,749 / 247,739,114, so you must diff adjacent rows (~79,635 txns for the last full day) rather than read it directly; raw use overstates daily activity by ~5 orders of magnitude. (2) Every pools(orderBy: ...) ranking query currently FAILS on this deployment — both orderBy: volumeUSD and orderBy: totalValueLockedUSD returned "bad indexers: {0x5af569b6…: Unavailable(too far behind), 0xdeb712db…: Unavailable(no status: indexer not available), 0xf92f430d…: BadResponse(expected value at line 1 column 1), 0xfeff9093…: Unavailable(too far behind)}" across 4 attempts, while _meta and uniswapDayDatas succeed against the same deployment in the same session. Only one indexer is at chainhead and it errors on the expensive full-scan sort over the Pool entity, so top-pool rankings are not retrievable from this subgraph ID right now.
entries.note: Canonical Uniswap V3 pool/swap/liquidity data on Polygon — pools, ticks, positions, and daily volume/TVL aggregates.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number } } pools(first: 3, orderBy: totalLiquidity, orderDirection: desc) { id name totalLiquidity totalSwapVolume swapsCount } swaps(first: 3, orderBy: timestamp, orderDirection: desc) { tokenInSym tokenOutSym tokenAmountIn tokenAmountOut valueUSD timestamp } }
entries.fieldWarning: Pool.totalSwapVolume and Pool.totalLiquidity are both junk. Ranking by totalSwapVolume puts "Balancer rETH Stable Pool" at 1.29e16 (~$12.9 quadrillion) from only 47,853 swaps, and 20wstETH-80AAVE at 4.4e13 (~$44 trillion) from 158,567 swaps (~$280M/swap) - decimals/pricing bug. Pool.totalLiquidity is equally unreliable: the same rETH pool reports totalLiquidity 0.628 despite 10,676 BPT of totalShares, while ranking by totalLiquidity puts "Balancer Morpho Aave v2 Boosted StablePool" at #1 with $21.4B TVL on just 40 swaps (boosted-pool / phantom-BPT double count) before dropping three orders of magnitude to $20.3M at #2. Swap.valueUSD is trustworthy - derive volume by summing it over a time window instead of using the Pool cumulative fields.
entries.note: Canonical Balancer V2 Ethereum mainnet subgraph — pools, swaps, joins/exits and token balances via the Vault, and the highest-fee deployment indexing that contract.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } markets(first: 3, orderBy: totalValueLockedUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id name inputToken { symbol decimals } borrowedToken { symbol decimals } totalValueLockedUSD totalDepositBalanceUSD totalBorrowBalanceUSD cumulativeBorrowUSD lltv borrowCount } }
entries.fieldWarning: totalValueLockedUSD (and the totalDepositBalanceUSD / totalBorrowBalanceUSD pair) is JUNK as a ranking field on this subgraph — do not orderBy it. The #1 row by TVL, "USDC / PAXG", reports $8.24B TVL but has only 12 borrows, inputTokenPriceUSD = "0" (no oracle price for PAXG), and totalCollateral of just 59578845182231419 raw = 0.0596 PAXG (~$0 at the reported price). Its totalDepositBalanceUSD and totalBorrowBalanceUSD are byte-identical ($8,241,403,229.19628490485129 for both), i.e. an impossible exact 100% utilization; same identical-pair defect on #2 "USDC / sdeUSD" ($3.2B). The value traces to a decimals/scale bug: TVL is computed as (loan-token supply / 10^loanDecimals) + (collateral * inputTokenPriceUSD), and for USDC/PAXG the raw totalSupply 8242668726125807 is divided by 1e6 to yield $8.24B while the collateral leg contributes 0 because the price is 0. The healthy row #3 "USDT / wstETH" checks out by the same formula (122,806 wstETH * $3,130 = $384.4M collateral + $134.7M supply = $519.1M TVL, deposits > borrows), which confirms the top two are corrupted rather than the formula. Contamination propagates upward: lendingProtocols reports totalValueLockedUSD $15.28B and totalBorrowBalanceUSD $13.53B (~88% protocol-wide utilization), both inflated well above Morpho Blue's real mainnet size by these bad markets. Rank/filter on borrowCount, transactionCount, or the raw totalSupply/totalBorrow/totalCollateral integers scaled by the correct token decimals instead, and drop any market with inputTokenPriceUSD == 0.
entries.note: Top-fee Ethereum mainnet indexer of the Morpho Blue singleton — use it for market state, supply/borrow/collateral positions, and liquidations.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number } } swaps(first: 3, orderBy: timestamp, orderDirection: desc) { id timestamp amount0 amount1 amountUSD pool { id token0 { symbol } token1 { symbol } } } }
entries.fieldWarning: totalValueLockedUSD is badly broken at every level and must not be used. PoolManager.totalValueLockedUSD returned 49795464148201426895533712 (~$5e25, tens of septillions of dollars) against totalVolumeUSD of only ~$146.6B — an impossible ratio. Pool.volumeUSD ranking is junk too: the top three pools by volumeUSD (USDC/RS $24.95B, USDC/HLZ $14.90B, USDC/YS $11.88B) each report txCount of just 34, and carry $2.7-3.2B totalValueLockedUSD — billions of dollars of volume and TVL from 34 transactions in unknown-token pools, i.e. bogus derived pricing on unpriced tokens. poolCount of 15,271,606 and txCount of 1,023,049,099 also suggest spam-pool inflation feeding the pricing logic. Use Swap.amountUSD (verified consistent) or filter to whitelisted/known tokens; treat totalValueLockedUSD, totalValueLockedETH and volumeUSD-based rankings as unreliable.
entries.note: Live Uniswap V4 PoolManager index on Base — pools, swaps, ticks, hooks, positions, and USD/ETH volume, fee and TVL rollups (day/hour) for V4 analytics.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } dexAmmProtocols { name network totalValueLockedUSD cumulativeVolumeUSD totalPoolCount } liquidityPools(first: 3, orderBy: cumulativeVolumeUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id name symbol totalValueLockedUSD cumulativeVolumeUSD cumulativeTotalRevenueUSD inputTokens { symbol decimals } } }
entries.fieldWarning: DexAmmProtocol.totalValueLockedUSD returned 1074789199590.95 (~$1.07 TRILLION) for SushiSwap on Ethereum — implausible by ~4 orders of magnitude (near total crypto market cap) and the classic Messari protocol-level TVL accumulation-drift bug. Per-pool LiquidityPool.totalValueLockedUSD values look sane ($200k-$626k), so only the protocol aggregate is junk. Never rank or report on the protocol totalValueLockedUSD; rank by cumulativeVolumeUSD instead.
entries.note: Messari-standard SushiSwap V2 AMM subgraph on Ethereum mainnet (dexAmmProtocol/liquidityPool/swap plus MasterChef staking entities) — good for pool TVL, volume, swaps and LP/reward analytics; verified live at block 25,979,461 indexing factory 0xc0aee478e3658e2610c5f7a4a2e1777ce9e4f2ac.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } bundles(first: 1) { ethPriceUSD } pools(first: 3, orderBy: volumeUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id feeTier volumeUSD totalValueLockedUSD txCount token0 { symbol } token1 { symbol } } }
entries.fieldWarning: No implausible magnitudes (TVL in single-digit millions, volumes in billions, ethPriceUSD ~$2.5k, no zero-volume top rows). BUT there is cross-indexer divergence on this subgraph ID: one call (a pools orderBy totalValueLockedUSD query issued without _meta) came back from a different server with materially different totals for the SAME pool 0x85149247691df622eaf1a8bd0cafd40bc45154a9 — txCount 16,663,991 / volumeUSD $11.93B / TVL $7.11M, versus txCount 10,187,270 / volumeUSD $2.83B / TVL $1.39M from deployment QmbTaWMFk4baXnoKQodnyYsFVKFNEiLsgZAe6eu2Sdj8Ef (reproduced twice). Cumulative volumeUSD/txCount and the totalValueLockedUSD ranking are therefore NOT stable across calls — the QmbTaWM deployment appears to undercount history (its TVL top-3 is USDC/WETH, USDC/WETH, WETH/WBTC while the other server ranks WETH/OP first at $8.77M). Always request _meta { deployment } and pin to one deployment before comparing or ranking on these cumulative fields.
entries.note: Canonical Uniswap V3 pool/swap/liquidity data on Optimism (27.5k pools, 78M txs) for DEX pricing, volume and LP position analytics.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } pools(first: 3, orderBy: volumeUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id feeTier volumeUSD txCount totalValueLockedUSD token0 { symbol } token1 { symbol } } }

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number } } swaps(first: 3, orderBy: timestamp, orderDirection: desc) { hash timestamp blockNumber amountInUSD amountOutUSD tokenIn { symbol } tokenOut { symbol } pool { name } } }
entries.fieldWarning: Both pool ranking fields are broken. (1) cumulativeVolumeUSD is junk: protocol-level reads 2.379e24 USD (septillions); ranking liquidityPools by it returns reUSD/sfrxUSD 1.384e24, sfrxUSD/sUSDe 5.04e23, sfrxUSD/scrvUSD 4.91e23 — and all three top rows have totalValueLockedUSD exactly "0", the classic junk-ranking signature. Mispricing clusters on sfrxUSD-paired pools. (2) Pool-level totalValueLockedUSD is also junk in the opposite direction: ranking by it puts cvxPrisma/Prisma first at $2.74B and Curve GEAR/ETH second at $776M, both tiny illiquid pools overvalued by orders of magnitude. Protocol totalValueLockedUSD of $4.92B only looks plausible by coincidence since it rolls up these pool values. Do not rank Curve pools by cumulativeVolumeUSD or totalValueLockedUSD on this deployment; use Swap/Deposit/Withdraw event amountInUSD/amountOutUSD/amountUSD or snapshot volume instead, and filter out pools with TVL 0.
entries.note: Messari DEX-AMM schema covering Curve's registries and pool factories on Ethereum mainnet — good for pool-level TVL, volume, swaps, liquidity events and protocol-wide financial snapshots across 1,308 pools.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } borrows(first: 3, orderBy: timestamp, orderDirection: desc) { id hash timestamp blockNumber amount amountUSD account { id } market { id name totalBorrow borrowCount } asset { symbol decimals } } }
entries.fieldWarning: All USD-denominated fields are broken and must not be used. LendingProtocol.totalValueLockedUSD reports $459.64 for the entire Morpho Blue deployment on Base across 4,302 pools — off by roughly seven orders of magnitude from reality. Token.lastPriceUSD and Market.inputTokenPriceUSD return "0" for every token sampled (USDC, WETH, eUSD, gUSD, KITE), and Borrow.amountUSD is "0" on every live event, including a 102 USDC borrow. Because prices are zero, USD ranking fields are junk: orderBy totalBorrowBalanceUSD put a $0.93 wUSDM/steakUSDC market with borrowCount 1 at rank #1, ahead of USDC/cbBTC with 433,934 borrows, and the #3 result had totalBorrowBalanceUSD of 1.18e-15. Also affected: totalDepositBalanceUSD, cumulativeBorrowUSD, cumulativeDepositUSD, cumulativeSupplySideRevenueUSD, cumulativeProtocolSideRevenueUSD, cumulativeTotalRevenueUSD. Use raw BigInt fields (amount, totalBorrow, totalSupply, totalCollateral) with the token's own decimals instead, and do not sum those across markets since units differ per market. Rank by activity counts (borrowCount, transactionCount) or timestamp, never by a USD field.
entries.note: Native Morpho Blue schema on Base (markets with lltv, totalSupply, totalBorrow, positions) — good for per-market lending/borrow state, LLTV tiers, and supplier/borrower positions; live and synced at Base block 51.3M.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number } } markets(first: 3, orderBy: totalDepositBalanceUSD, orderDirection: desc, where: {isActive: true}) { id name inputToken { symbol decimals } inputTokenPriceUSD totalValueLockedUSD totalDepositBalanceUSD totalBorrowBalanceUSD cumulativeBorrowUSD transactionCount } }
entries.note: Messari-schema Aave V3 lending data on Arbitrum — per-market TVL, supply/borrow rates, positions and liquidations by reserve token.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } markets(first: 3, orderBy: totalDepositBalanceUSD, orderDirection: desc, where: {isActive: true}) { id name inputToken { symbol decimals } inputTokenPriceUSD totalValueLockedUSD totalDepositBalanceUSD totalBorrowBalanceUSD cumulativeBorrowUSD borrowCount } }
entries.fieldWarning: No implausible values: USD magnitudes are billions (not trillions), stablecoin price ~$1.00, LST prices near ETH, and no top-ranked row has zero activity. One caveat worth knowing: totalValueLockedUSD returns exactly the same number as totalDepositBalanceUSD on every market (it is a mirror of deposits and is NOT net of borrows), so do not treat it as an independent TVL metric or sum it alongside borrows. Also note weETH ranks #1 by deposits while showing only ~$141k of borrows — that is real Aave behavior (collateral-only asset with a near-zero borrow cap), not a decimals bug, but it makes totalDepositBalanceUSD a poor proxy for market utilization.
entries.note: Canonical Aave V3 lending market data on Ethereum mainnet — reserves, rates, user positions, borrows/supplies and liquidations.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } markets(first: 3, orderBy: totalDepositBalanceUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id name isActive inputToken { symbol decimals } inputTokenPriceUSD totalValueLockedUSD totalDepositBalanceUSD totalBorrowBalanceUSD rates { side type rate } } }
entries.fieldWarning: Minor: for the top market (Moonwell USDC) totalBorrowBalanceUSD ($8,779,985.90) slightly EXCEEDS totalDepositBalanceUSD / totalValueLockedUSD ($8,721,481.17), i.e. implied utilization of 100.7%, which is not physically possible in a Compound-style pool — the Messari deposit/TVL figure appears to be underlying cash net of reserves rather than cash+borrows, so per-market totalValueLockedUSD should not be used as a strict upper bound on borrows or to compute utilization. Protocol-level totals are self-consistent ($38.07M TVL vs $24.52M borrows, 64% utilization) and nothing is in the trillions. Also note markets(orderBy: totalDepositBalanceUSD) includes markets with isActive=false (Moonwell WETH ranked #3), so filter on isActive: true if you want live markets only.
entries.note: Messari-schema lending subgraph for Moonwell on Base: live per-market deposit/borrow balances, rates, liquidations, and per-account positions across all 21 mToken markets.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } marketplaces { id name network tradeCount cumulativeTradeVolumeETH collectionCount cumulativeUniqueTraders totalRevenueETH } trades(first: 3, orderBy: timestamp, orderDirection: desc) { id timestamp blockNumber priceETH tokenId amount strategy buyer seller collection { id name symbol nftStandard tradeCount cumulativeTradeVolumeETH } } }
entries.fieldWarning: Freshness trap, not a decimals trap: _meta reports chainhead (block 25,979,492) but the newest Trade entity is block 25,592,621 — roughly 54 days stale — and marketplaceDailySnapshots skip from day id 20260 straight to 20656, a ~396-day window with zero recorded trades. The most recent snapshot shows dailyTradedItemCount 3 / dailyActiveTraders 4, implausibly low for OpenSea. Root cause is that the subgraph tracks Seaport 1.1 (0x00000000006c3852cbef3e08e8df289169ede581), deprecated in favor of Seaport 1.4/1.5 (0x00000000000001ad428e4906aE43D8F9852d0dD6) and 1.6 (0x0000000000000068F116a894984e2DB1123eB395), so current OpenSea volume is not captured. Treat all cumulative* fields as frozen historical totals, never as live metrics, and do not trust _meta alone as a liveness signal for this subgraph. Numerically the values are self-consistent (2,617,514 ETH over 13.9M trades = 0.188 ETH avg; totalRevenueETH is 5.99% of volume, matching 2.5% marketplace + ~3.5% creator fees) and the schema exposes no USD or TVL fields at all, so the totalValueLockedUSD/profitUSD traps do not apply here.
entries.note: Messari-standard NFT marketplace schema for Seaport on Ethereum: trades, collections, order fulfillments, items, and daily marketplace/collection snapshots (13.9M trades, 2.6M ETH volume); note it tracks Seaport 1.1 (0x...ede581), not the 1.6 contract in the hint, and the reported fee comes from a separate generic NFT-sales deployment (QmQy71UkrogfDmfkR14QHpaQTEKKKnycVgwt8dY1iFZAL2) that indexes the 1.6 address.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number } } markets(first: 3, orderBy: totalDepositBalanceUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id name isActive totalValueLockedUSD totalDepositBalanceUSD totalBorrowBalanceUSD inputToken { symbol } } }
entries.fieldWarning: isActive is unreliable on this deployment — the three largest real markets (WBTC $67M, USDT $32M, WETH $31M) all return isActive: false, so `where: {isActive: true}` silently drops the biggest markets and returned only 2 rows for first:3. Do not filter on isActive; filter on totalDepositBalanceUSD_gt instead. Secondary note (by schema design, not a bug): totalValueLockedUSD is exactly equal to totalDepositBalanceUSD on every row — it is gross deposits, not deposits minus borrows, so don't read it as net liquidity. USD magnitudes themselves are plausible (no trillions, no zero-volume top rows).
entries.note: Canonical Aave V3 lending market data on Polygon — reserves, rates, user positions, borrows/repays and liquidations.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } liquidityPools(first: 3, orderBy: cumulativeVolumeUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id name symbol totalValueLockedUSD cumulativeVolumeUSD longOpenInterestUSD shortOpenInterestUSD totalOpenInterestUSD openPositionCount cumulativePositionCount cumulativeUniqueUsers } }
entries.fieldWarning: openPositionCount (and longPositionCount 1,220,113 / shortPositionCount 904,361) are junk — position closes are not decrementing the counters. Confirmed with a second query: cumulativePositionCount 2,908,933 − closedPositionCount 784,459 = openPositionCount 2,124,474 exactly, i.e. ~73% of every position ever opened is still counted "open" while totalOpenInterestUSD is only $237,036 (~$0.11 of open interest per supposedly-open position). Do not use these counters for open-position analytics; totalValueLockedUSD, cumulativeVolumeUSD and the OI USD fields looked plausible.
entries.note: Core GMX V1 perps subgraph on Arbitrum — tracks Vault positions, swaps, liquidations and fees; highest query-fee deployment for the GMX Vault contract.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } protocols(first: 1) { name network totalValueLockedUSD cumulativeDepositVolumeUSD cumulativeUniqueDepositors totalPoolCount } pools(first: 3, orderBy: totalValueLockedUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id name symbol type totalValueLockedUSD cumulativeDepositVolumeUSD cumulativeWithdrawalVolumeUSD cumulativeUniqueDepositors inputTokenBalances inputTokens { symbol decimals lastPriceUSD } } }
entries.fieldWarning: Token.lastPriceUSD is broken for bEIGEN: it returns "0" for token in strategy 0xacb55c530acdb2849e6d4f36992cd8c9d50ed8f7 even though that pool reports totalValueLockedUSD $316.6M against 399,414,117 bEIGEN (an implied ~$0.793/token). Any calculation doing inputTokenBalances x lastPriceUSD will value bEIGEN at zero; use totalValueLockedUSD or inputTokenBalancesUSD instead. Secondary caveat (not a bug): protocols.totalPoolCount = 34,809 is dominated by per-staker EigenPods, not strategies, so it is not comparable to a strategy count.
entries.note: EigenLayer core restaking on Ethereum mainnet: per-strategy and per-EigenPod TVL, deposits, and queued/completed withdrawals with depositor accounts and daily/hourly snapshots.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } liquidityPools(first: 3, orderBy: cumulativeVolumeUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id name symbol totalValueLockedUSD cumulativeVolumeUSD cumulativeTotalRevenueUSD inputTokens { symbol decimals } } }
entries.fieldWarning: Values are plausible (protocol TVL $13.6M, no trillions; every top-ranked row has non-zero volume; fee take 0.05%/0.30% matches Velodrome tiers) — but cross-call consistency is not: repeated queries for pool 0x8134a2fd (vAMMV2-USDC/VELO) returned totalValueLockedUSD $124.5k / cumulativeVolumeUSD $278.7M on the canonical deployment QmbNRb..., versus $934.2k / $218.1M on another call, meaning the gateway sometimes routes to a lagging indexer. Always request _meta { block { number } deployment } alongside any TVL/volume figure and discard responses from a stale block. Secondary note: vAMMV2-USDC/VELO shows $3.01M cumulative revenue on $279.8M volume (~1.08% effective take), well above the 0.30% volatile-pool fee seen on OP/USDC — likely custom/dynamic fee periods (_customFeeApplied exists in the schema) but treat that pool's revenue figure with caution.
entries.note: Messari DEX-AMM schema over Velodrome Finance V2 on Optimism (1,389 pools) — good for pool TVL/volume, swaps, deposits/withdraws, gauges, and daily/hourly financial snapshots.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number timestamp } } dexAmmProtocols { name network totalValueLockedUSD cumulativeVolumeUSD totalPoolCount } liquidityPools(first: 3, orderBy: cumulativeVolumeUSD, orderDirection: desc) { id name symbol totalValueLockedUSD cumulativeVolumeUSD inputTokens { symbol decimals } } }
entries.fieldWarning: Two independent problems. (1) STALE: _meta.block is 21586870 / timestamp 1649695710 = 2022-04-11, over four years behind Gnosis chainhead as of 2026-09-14 — the deployment is stalled/failed, not merely lagging, and latest swaps() also top out at that same block. (2) ALL USD FIELDS ARE JUNK ZEROS: dexAmmProtocols.totalValueLockedUSD = 0, cumulativeVolumeUSD = 0, every liquidityPools.totalValueLockedUSD = 0 and cumulativeVolumeUSD = 0, and swaps.amountInUSD / amountOutUSD = 0 (e.g. a swap of 10.71 WXDAI -> 10.707 USDC reports amountInUSD "0"). Ordering by cumulativeVolumeUSD or totalValueLockedUSD is therefore meaningless — every row ties at 0 and the "top" rows are arbitrary. Only native-unit fields are trustworthy: inputTokenBalances and amountIn/amountOut are plausible and consistent with token decimals (e.g. wxDAI/USDC/USDT pool holds ~34.0M USDT (6dp), ~47.7M USDC (6dp), ~43.2M WXDAI (18dp)). Do not use any *USD field from this subgraph.
entries.note: Messari-schema Curve AMM data on Gnosis (liquidityPools, swaps, deposits/withdrawals, TVL/volume snapshots) — best for tracking xDAI/USDC/USDT and GNO-family stable pools.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number } } deposits(first: 3, orderBy: blockNumber, orderDirection: desc) { id blockNumber timestamp amount amountUSD hash } borrows(first: 3, orderBy: blockNumber, orderDirection: desc) { id blockNumber timestamp amount amountUSD } liquidates(first: 2, orderBy: blockNumber, orderDirection: desc) { blockNumber amountUSD profitUSD } }
entries.fieldWarning: Multiple severe problems. (1) markets and lendingProtocols return EMPTY arrays on every attempt (with and without where/orderBy, plain first:2) — the headline TVL entities have no data at all, so totalValueLockedUSD / totalDepositBalanceUSD / totalBorrowBalanceUSD are unqueryable. (2) Dangling non-null refs: traversing deposit.market or deposit.asset fails with "Null value resolved for non-null field `market`" / "`asset`", so any relation-joining query errors outright. (3) profitUSD is a textbook decimals bug — a liquidate with amountUSD 0.0538 reports profitUSD -49,362,333,015,693,495.36 (~18 orders of magnitude too large, and negative); another with amountUSD 1.357 reports profitUSD -1,298,935.71. Do not use profitUSD. (4) Content is ~2 years stale despite _meta sitting at chainhead, and history is pruned (block:{number:125235664} → "bad indexers: missing block 125235664, latest 156918103" from the single serving indexer 0xf92f430d…a6d4). Treat this subgraph as responsive-but-unusable for Aave V3 Optimism market state.

entries.fieldWarning: No bad data, but one value needs context: the top-ranked market by deposits (Compound V3 USDC - Wrapped BTC) returns totalBorrowBalanceUSD=0 and borrowCount=0. This is structurally correct for Compound V3 (collateral assets are supply-only; only the base asset is borrowable), not a junk ranking field. totalValueLockedUSD is trustworthy here — it exactly equals totalDepositBalanceUSD per market and is in the hundreds of millions, not trillions.

entries.fieldWarning: STALE ENTITY (not a decimals bug): networkStakerBalanceCheckpoints is frozen. Its newest row is block 20102485 / blockTime 1718518403 (2024-06-16) while the subgraph itself is indexed to block 25979487 — about 5.88M blocks (~2 years) of no new checkpoints. So rETHExchangeRate (1108864467208237612 = 1.1089 ETH/rETH), totalRETHSupply (504356249756802560548039 = 504,356 rETH), stakerETHInProtocol (559262724169721692237541 = 559,262 ETH) and stakersWithAnRETHBalance (17988) read fine and cross-check correctly against each other (504356 x 1.1089 = 559,281, matches), but they describe mid-2024, NOT today. Do not use this entity for current rETH exchange rate or TVL. RocketPoolProtocol.lastNetworkStakerBalanceCheckPoint and stakerBalanceCheckpoints inherit the same staleness. Live entities (rocketETHTransactions at head, minipools with nodeDepositBlockTime 1765144583 = 2025-12) are current, so this is a broken handler for one event, not a dead subgraph.

entries.exampleQuery: { _meta { block { number } } reserves(first: 3, orderBy: totalATokenSupply, orderDirection: desc, where: {isActive: true}) { symbol decimals totalATokenSupply totalCurrentVariableDebt availableLiquidity utilizationRate liquidityRate variableBorrowRate lastUpdateTimestamp } }
entries.fieldWarning: RANKING TRAP: orderBy totalATokenSupply sorts on the RAW BigInt, which is NOT decimals-normalized, so the ordering is economically meaningless across reserves with different decimals. A follow-up query confirmed it: USDC (decimals 6) has totalATokenSupply 181638056952429 = ~181.6M USDC and cbBTC (decimals 8) has 281355479537 = ~2,813 BTC, both far larger in USD than GHO's ~1.42M, yet both sort BELOW GHO because GHO carries 18 decimals and therefore a bigger raw integer. Any size ranking must divide by `decimals` (and multiply by price) client-side, or use a per-decimals filter. Secondary inconsistency: GHO's stored utilizationRate is 0.65303906, but its own debt/(debt+availableLiquidity) works out to ~0.842 - the field appears stale or computed on a different base for that reserve. WETH (0.79928 vs ~0.808), cbETH (0.00410 vs ~0.00435), USDC (0.84373 vs ~0.872) and cbBTC (0.03296 vs ~0.0347) all reconcile closely, so GHO is the outlier; prefer deriving utilization from the debt and liquidity fields rather than trusting the stored one.

"Lido", QmTCRJGmwf... "Lido Ethereum"), so no live Lido mainnet fallback was found on the network either. probe.saw: Queries execute cleanly (valid schema, no GraphQL errors, no indexing errors) but the subgraph contains ZERO entities. Deployment QmNs1YDpRPdHFcXdyZ9nwDQAx74hwuWDyULE74rejd4THP is synced to Ethereum mainnet chainhead (block 25,979,495, timestamp 1789434671 = 2026-09-14, advancing live between calls) and _meta.hasIndexingErrors=false — yet every one of the 14 top-level entity collections returns an empty array: markets, marketStates, assets, assetAmounts, transactions, lockingEvents, votingEvents, voteSnapshots, poolVoteTotals, governanceEvents, poolMetaDatas, ptToPies, ytToMarkets, bundles, pySnapshots. Tested with and without orderBy, so this is not the zero-match-where + orderBy timeout trap. Market is an immutable entity, so rows could not have been deleted — nothing was ever written. get_deployment_30day_query_counts confirms 0 queries and 0 data points over 30 days, i.e. nobody is using this deployment. Verdict: the indexer process is ALIVE but the subgraph is functionally DEAD as a data source — no useful query is possible against it. Only _meta returns real values. Marked works=false because no entity data was returned; do not catalog a query against this subgraph ID.

Only the _meta query executed successfully, returning block 121938508, deployment QmUwBMokciw5TY5kHYtqMXXuZdymDy2knYpRxHwqiy85od, hasIndexingErrors: true. EVERY entity query failed at the gateway with `bad indexers: {0xf92f430dd8567b0d466358c79594ab58d919a6d4: BadResponse(no attestation: indexing_error)}` — tried pools orderBy volumeUSD, pools orderBy txCount, bare pools(first:3){id volumeUSD}, and swaps orderBy timestamp, both with and without `subgraphError: allow`; all rejected. A historical-block read (block:{number:121900000}) failed differently: `Unavailable(missing block: 121900000, latest: 121938508)`, i.e. history is pruned, so there is no earlier block to fall back to. A single indexer serves this deployment and it will not attest entity responses. Freshness cross-check against a BSC RPC: chainhead 121940000 vs subgraph head 121938508 = ~1492 blocks behind, so the deployment is tracking chainhead — it is not stalled, but it is unusable for data: no entity field can be read through the gateway. Treat this subgraph as NOT alive for querying.
